strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas rolling var/std catastrophic cancellation: the buggy revision (446d8098f4f2) lets the online Welford update produce wrong/negative variances on a window containing 99999999999999999; the PR replaces the test with test_rolling_var_correctness, which fails on the buggy revision and passes on the fixed one. Build pandas from source at the buggy commit (Cython extensions in pandas/_libs/window/aggregations.pyx must be recompiled), then run the PR's test file against it.

pinned_because: NumPy is documented in README.md with no constraint and no era ceiling; left unpinned, so the strategy chooses the latest NumPy compatible with the buggy commit's source tree; this is a choice, not a documented requirement
Cython is documented in README.md with no constraint; installed unpinned for the source build, a choice not a documented requirement
Python version not stated by the evidence (null); use the interpreter the checkout's pyproject.toml supports

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py::test_rolling_var_correctness (parametrized over func, values, window, ddof, expected_values from the PR diff; includes the 99999999999999999 var/std cases and the 1.3e17 std case)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 446d8098f4f2, the test_rolling_var_correctness cases involving the 99999999999999999 series fail in tm.assert_series_equal because the computed var/std values are wrong (zeros, or negative variances from cancellation) rather than the expected 5e33 / 7.071068e16 / 0.7071068 values. On the fixed revision (the PR's merge), all parametrized cases of test_rolling_var_correctness pass. The transition fail-to-pass is the success criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run Series([99999999999999999, 1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1]).rolling(2).std(ddof=1) on buggy and fixed builds and compare with the test's expected list; used only to confirm the build is the right revision, not graded.

input_output_examples.input: Series([99999999999999999, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 1]).rolling(2).var() with third value case giving 5e+33 first window

risks: The defect is a float64 cancellation effect, so it should reproduce on x86_64 Linux with standard IEEE arithmetic; the old test was xfail on arm, power and riscv64 (GH 38921), so on those architectures the buggy behaviour may differ and the transition may not occur. Run on x86_64.
The build must be from the buggy commit's Cython sources; a stale or prebuilt wheel of a different pandas version will not reproduce the defect and the test may pass on both revisions.

The new test also includes a case with values near 1e-36 to 1e-73 and a 1e10 case; if the buggy revision fails only on the 1e17 cases, the failure still counts, but the assertion message will name whichever case fails first.

The test uses tm.assert_series_equal with atol=1e-55 and rtol default; the tolerance interacts with the expected values, so a loose or absent tolerance in a different pandas version could hide the failure.
The PR diff removes is_platform_arm/power/riscv64 imports and the xfail marker, so the test runs on every platform; a platform where the buggy revision happens to be exact would show no transition.
The original test test_rolling_var_numerical_issues is not present on the fixed revision, so select the new test name rather than the old one.
The evidence does not state a Python version, a compiler, or a BLAS/threading setting; these are unknown and left to the defaults of the buggy checkout.
An empty entry appeared in reproduction_risks in the evidence; it was ignored.
The 'third value' parametrisation of the old test (third_value=1 vs 2) is not reproduced verbatim by the new test; the 1e17 cases in the new test use explicit value lists instead.

oracle.tolerance: atol=1e-55 with pandas default rtol in tm.assert_series_equal (assert_almost_equal); tolerance is stated by the PR diff, not by the evidence beyond that
oracle.why: Expected values are hand-listed to 7-8 significant figures and the comparison goes through the tolerance-based tm.assert_series_equal, so a pass on the fixed build depends on the explicit atol.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 446d8098f4f2 the 99999999999999999 var/std cases return zeros or negative variances because the online Welford update cancels catastrophically after the 1e17 value leaves or enters the window; assert_series_equal then sees values that differ from the expected 5e33 / 7.07e16 / 0.707 entries and raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR's fixed revision the num_consecutive_same_value logic is removed from add_var and calc_var and the numerically_unstable handling is added, so the same cases produce the expected values within atol=1e-55 and the GH 42064 zero-equality check also holds; all parametrized cases pass.
